column1: # Census of state and Party media items on Nvidia and its chips, Jul 2025 to Nov 2026, held (saved under research/primary) or found. One row per item (an item carried by several pages is one row; extra carriers in col 10). Built on Nov 23, 2026 from: every saved page whose address is a central state or Party outlet (a scan of the saved pages' addresses), the rows of the project's earlier searches, those searches' notes of what they had not reached, and further searches made for this table. Scope: central Party and state media (People's Daily group incl. Overseas Edition, People.cn, Global Times/Huanqiu, China Economic Weekly, the Party members' paper; Xinhua group incl. Economic Information Daily, Reference News, Xinhua Finance; China Media Group incl. CCTV, CGTN, Yuyuan Tantian; Guangming Daily group incl. Zhonghua Dushubao; Economic Daily; China Daily; Qiushi; Study Times; Science and Technology Daily) and one city Party paper (Beijing Daily). Commercial outlets (The Paper, Sina, IT Home, Eastmoney, Tencent News) appear only as carriers. Columns: 1 date = the page's own publication date (Beijing time) | 2 outlet = who published the words | 3 kind = signed commentary | unsigned commentary | news | interview | social post | official text carried | analysis | notice | 4 stance toward buying Nvidia chips = warns (discourages buying or using) | welcomes (favours imports or Nvidia's presence) | mixed (both in one item) | neutral (reports without advice) | self-reliance (stresses home-made chips without advice on buying) | other | 5 speaker = whose words the key sentence is | 6 key sentence = exact words from the saved page (checked against the saved copy by script) | 7 saved id of the page that carries the key sentence | 8 held = saved and read | found = known, not saved | 9 original? = original outlet page | outlet's own channel on a platform | relay (another site) | 10 other carriers (saved ids) | 11 the row's place in the list of the earlier search it came from, as list:line (- where it was found another way) | 12 note

# Added Nov 24, 2026: rows 43 to 75, found by a second search for this table, by web searches with other words, the outlets' list pages and links on saved pages, and title-word scans of the e-papers of People's Daily, its Overseas Edition, Guangming Daily and Economic Daily; for Jul 31 to Sept 24, 2025 a second search of those weeks, and after Sept 24, 2025 a sample from searches and links, not a census of those papers (the note of each row says how it was found). Rows 30 and 42 replaced and rows 15, 17 and 34 annotated the same day. Stance rule applied to rows 43 to 75 and checked against rows 1 to 42: warns = the item, in its own words or a speaker's it quotes, says Nvidia's chips carry security risks, or that Nvidia must prove them safe, or argues against buying or using them; mixed = that, together with words that Nvidia or American chipmakers are welcome or that imports may resume; a sentence that only reports or predicts buyers' reluctance is not a warning. Rows 49, 52 and 64 are coded otherwise than the second search coded them, as each row's note says. A baseline for Jan 2024 to Jun 2025, in these columns and by this rule but gathered later by other routes (web searches, the Yuyuan Tantian index on CCTV's site, a title-word scan of four papers) and not a census, is kept apart in tables/state_media_baseline_2024_2025h1.tsv (49 items, 1 warns); its rows are not counted here. Rows 9, 10, 11, 27, 37, 48, 54, 55, 67 and 74 were recoded on Nov 25, 2026 after two blind second coders and a third reader; an item that carries the regulator's own words on the chips' security or its demand for proof counts as warning, as row 13 counts for the commentary it carries.
